name: Sekiro™: Shadows Die Twice - GOTY Edition

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a 40 fps cap is the sweet spot for Sekiro on Deck — it feels fluid and consistent, and the 40 Hz mode eliminates tearing. FSR at 1024x640 recovers sharpness well and keeps the GPU comfortably within budget across all areas.

profiles.Summary: Sekiro runs very well on the Steam Deck, benefiting from its relatively modest PC requirements and FromSoftware's efficient engine — expect smooth 60 fps in most areas at medium-to-high settings. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, making it an excellent handheld experience out of the box.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (GTX 760–970 range, well within Deck capability), the game's ProtonDB platinum rating, and FromSoftware's historically efficient engine. On your first run, check frame rate in Ashina Castle — if it dips below your cap there, reduce Shadow Quality one step.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load minimal; 7 W TDP and a 30 fps cap extend battery significantly. Sekiro remains very playable at 30 fps since its combat is reaction-based and consistent frame pacing matters more than raw frame rate.

KnownIssues: The game targets a locked 60 fps by design and has no built-in frame rate cap option, so Deck-level frame limiting is essential for battery and stability.
Some cutscenes and dense areas (e.g. Ashina Castle during late-game invasions) can cause brief frame dips.
Online connectivity (Dragonrot/NPC state sync) may require Proton Experimental for reliable network functionality.
No native ultrawide or resolution scaling options in-game; all upscaling must be handled via the Deck's FSR overlay.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full native 1280x800 at max settings is achievable in most areas, but late-game zones like Fountainhead Palace and Ashina Castle (invasion phase) may dip into the high 40s — keep the 60 fps cap to avoid GPU thrash. Battery life is short at full TDP; keep a charger handy.

Optimal.Notes: A slight render resolution reduction to 1152x720 with FSR keeps the GPU well within its headroom for a near-locked 60 fps, which is ideal for Sekiro's demanding combat timing. High textures preserve visual fidelity while medium shadows and AO balance image quality with performance.

profiles.Summary: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice runs well on the Steam Deck OLED, achieving stable 60 fps in most areas at medium-to-high settings thanks to its modest PC requirements and DirectX 11 engine. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, making it an excellent handheld experience with no major compatibility hurdles.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 970 recommended, well within the Deck's GTX 1050 Ti-class GPU) and the game's ProtonDB platinum rating. On first run, check frame pacing in Ashina Castle or Ashina Outskirts (the busiest areas) and drop to the Optimal profile if you see dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render resolution dropped to 960x600 with FSR upscaling to ease GPU load; 7 W TDP and 900 MHz GPU clock keep thermals and power draw minimal. Motion Blur and DoF are disabled to reduce GPU overhead and improve perceived clarity at lower resolution.

KnownIssues: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparison.
Some FromSoftware titles using similar engines can exhibit minor stutters during shader compilation on first launch under Proton.
The game requires a network connection check on first launch which may cause a brief delay under Proton.
HDR output may not be active in-game despite the OLED panel's capability; the game does not natively support HDR.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at max settings with no TDP or GPU clock limits; Sekiro's relatively modest PC requirements mean the Deck can handle this comfortably in most areas, though dense outdoor scenes like Ashina Outskirts may dip toward 60 fps. Motion Blur is left off as it can obscure enemy attack animations, which is a gameplay disadvantage.
